prize_parts.citation: for the development of reversible-terminator sequencing-by-synthesis chemistry enabling massively parallel DNA sequencing

statement.case_for: I keep B055 for Balasubramanian and Klenerman. After the first round it is still the candidate that best matches the criteria members stated in common: a defined chemical scheme (reversible terminator nucleotides, cleavable fluorophores, polymerase incorporation, clonal clusters on a surface), independent use on many instruments for two decades, and an impact that is easy to explain. The chair asks whether the citation can be anchored in the terminator chemistry for the Cambridge pair. I think it can if the wording says reversible-terminator sequencing-by-synthesis chemistry and does not name genomics or sequencing in general; that wording also answers the technology objection, because the discovery claimed is a molecular design and not an instrument. I have not moved my configuration since round 1. I did test it against B052, the strongest rival, and the round-1 exchange has not changed my view that B052 needs a settled attribution and a clearer clinical record before I would put it first.
statement.case_against: The category risk is real: sequencing can be read as technology or biology, and the standard has to be applied equally to B021, B052 and B063, which I accept. Attribution is lossy. Ju's terminator chemistry, Mayer's clonal amplification and Rothberg's 454 platform each have a claim, and I still cannot verify the internal priority picture from the material supplied. Finally, the first round did not converge: B055 has two explicit supporters, B052 has two, and a two-person single-part prize with that support does not yet look like five votes.

responses.point: Chabes configures B055 for Balasubramanian and Klenerman with a citation on reversible-terminator chemistry, and pairs it with base editing for Liu alone as a second part.
responses.response: We agree on the first part and on its citation. I do not support the pairing with B021. Base editing is young, long-term safety and bystander editing are still being measured, and you yourself concede that omitting Komor, Gaudelli, Nishida and Kondo is a real attribution cost. A two-part prize that attaches a less mature, contested part to the most mature candidate on the list weakens the case that is strongest. I would rather have B055 stand alone and let B021 be judged in a later year.

responses.point: Linke now leads with B052 for Crews, Deshaies and Handa, as one induced-proximity principle with independent reproduction, and accepts that no PROTAC drug is approved and that Ciulli, Gray, Sakamoto, Kim and Ito are left out.
responses.response: The principle is clear and I rank B052 as my first alternative. But your own reservations are my concerns: the PROTAC and cereblon-glue lineages are close to two discoveries, and the structural work that explains how ternary complexes form, which I weight heavily, is largely Ciulli's, who is not in your trio. On your maturity question, I would be comfortable if the clinical record included an approved degrader, but a prize for the principle alone, with the structural basis credited to someone else, is the most contestable of the leading citations. B055 does not have that problem.

responses.point: Aili wants the B052 citation to name both PROTAC heterobifunctional degraders and cereblon-directed glues, so that Crews, Deshaies and Handa cover both lineages in one citation.
responses.response: Naming both lineages is more honest than a one-principle citation, but it makes my attribution concern sharper, not weaker. A citation that names two mechanisms and credits three people where the key VHL structural work and the Gray, Sakamoto and Ito contributions are missing invites the question of who discovered what. If the committee does move to B052 I would support your wording over Linke's, and I would ask that Ciulli be considered before Deshaies, but I do not move my first choice for it.

responses.point: Brzezinski asked whether I could name three non-replaceable people for the mesoporous silica credit and said that a six-name field makes a three-person cut arbitrary.
responses.response: That is a fair test, and I could not pass it: the Mobil group, the independent FSM-16 work and the later SBA and KIT contributions cannot be cut to three without an arbitrary decision. That is the reason I dropped B043 as my first choice and moved to B055, where two names carry the chemistry. I keep B043 only as an alternative, not as a proposal. I also note your own B054 has a clean two-name credit, but the question whether it established more than Marcus-theory experiments had already shown, which you raise yourself, is one I cannot resolve either.

uncertainties: Whether the committee will treat reversible-terminator sequencing-by-synthesis as chemistry rather than technology or biology, and apply the same standard to B021, B052 and B063.
Whether Ju's terminator chemistry or Mayer's clonal amplification are strong enough to change the credit; I cannot verify priority from the supplied material.
Whether a majority can form around any two-person or three-person configuration, given six different first choices after round 1.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict with any shortlisted candidate has arisen. I remain a Stockholm University colleague of Secretary Peter Brzezinski, which is not a connection to any candidate. My field (porous materials and electron crystallography) is adjacent to B043, which is now only an alternative, and I do not let that adjacency drive my configuration.
